content.text: Review all the unit tests.  Create a pr removing any test that is duplicate or no longer needed.  Add GitHub inline comments explaining your reasoning and prove it isn't needed.  If you are uncertain, don't remove it. After you have created the pr, analyze the token use of this thread

I’ll inventory the unit tests, remove only cases I can prove are redundant, and verify the remaining coverage. Then I’ll create the PR, add inline comments with the evidence for each removal, and analyze this thread’s token use. I’m using the repository’s PR adherence skill for the final review.

The unit suites span Roam, Obsidian, the website, shared packages, and repository scripts. I’ll compare each candidate’s inputs, setup, and assertions with the coverage that would remain. GitHub CLI authentication is invalid, so I’m checking the connected GitHub app as a publishing path.

The inventory contains 73 unit-test files and 625 test declarations, including parameterized cases. I found one pair with identical bodies in the same suite. The baseline validation gate also fails on existing Obsidian type errors, so I’ll run the unit suites separately and disclose that blocker in a draft PR.

I’ve removed three tests, totaling 23 lines. One exactly duplicates a retained test; the other two repeat checks already implied by stronger assertions using the same fixtures. For each removal, I deliberately introduced the regression it guarded against and confirmed the retained test failed. All temporary production changes have been restored.

I’m now running the final suites, scope and standards checks, and the fresh-context delegated review required by the repository.
